column15: notes

Infrastructure. Homebrew runs on Linux (script) but on Linux the system package manager (pacman, apt, dnf) is the infrastructure analogue. On Windows the analogue is winget (Scoop and Chocolatey optional). No Windows build. Evidence: https://docs.brew.sh/Homebrew-on-Linux

Infrastructure (Node.js plus npm). Current line shown to match the macOS brew node formula. LTS ids are winget OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS, scoop main/nodejs-lts, choco nodejs-lts. Debian stable and Fedora ship older majors. Snap node is published by the OpenJS Foundation (verified). On Linux the npm package pulls in nodejs. Manual download: https://nodejs.org/en/download.

Infrastructure. Debian apt uv exists only in forky/sid (0.9.x, lags). snap astral-uv is not published by Astral. Script installs support uv self update. Evidence: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/

Infrastructure (interactive catalog). Debian trixie ships 0.60 (lags). Arch, Fedora, winget current. Manual download: https://github.com/junegunn/fzf/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/junegunn/fzf#installation

apt and dnf current only from the vendor repo at cli.github.com/packages (distro gh lags). snap is unofficial. Manual download: https://github.com/cli/cli/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/cli/cli#installation
Vendor documents npm (project-local or global). Arch extra package also tracks releases. Evidence: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/install-and-update/
No Debian or Fedora package. Arch extra is current. Evidence: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/getting_started/installation/
Arch extra lags one patch. Script installs support bun upgrade. Evidence: https://bun.com/docs/installation
Fedora ships pnpm 10.x (lags current 12.x). macOS catalog uses npm. Evidence: https://pnpm.io/installation
jq snap is old and unofficial. Manual download: https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases. Evidence: https://jqlang.org/download/

Arch pacman yq and Debian/Ubuntu apt yq are the unrelated Python yq, use go-yq on Arch and snap/binary on Debian. snap publisher is Mike Farah. Manual download: https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/mikefarah/yq#install
Command: rg. Manual download: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep#installation
Command: fd (Debian/Ubuntu install it as fdfind). Manual download: https://github.com/sharkdp/fd/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/sharkdp/fd#installation
apt package only in Debian 13+ and Ubuntu 24.04+ (older there). Evidence: https://just.systems/man/en/packages.html
choco lags (0.9.0). snap is published by the author. Manual download: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck#installing

Not packaged in Debian, Ubuntu or Fedora. The vendor download script only fetches the binary into the current folder, so aiup does not use it. Manual download: https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/blob/main/docs/install.md

apt and dnf use Anthropic's signed repo at downloads.claude.ai (stable and latest channels). Native script self-updates. winget and repos do not. Snap claude-code is not Anthropic-published. Evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup
winget GitHub.Copilot is the GitHub-published MSI. AUR copilot-cli is the unrelated AWS Copilot. Evidence: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli

Arch extra openai-codex lags npm by a few releases. AUR openai-codex-bin tracks npm. winget publisher is OpenAI. Manual download: https://github.com/openai/codex/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/openai/codex
Binary agy. Windows CMD variant install.cmd also documented. winget publisher is Google. Evidence: https://antigravity.google/docs/getting-started?tab=cli

Binary grok. install.ps1 confirmed served by x.ai. xAI install page blocked automated fetch, so the ps1 command comes from the served script plus winget xAI.GrokBuild (publisher xAI Corp.). Evidence: https://docs.x.ai/build/overview
Sunset for personal accounts (Antigravity CLI replaces it). No winget package. choco gemini-cli is stale (0.27.2) and omitted. Evidence: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli
pi.dev scripts install the same npm package into a managed prefix. winget publisher is Earendil Inc. Evidence: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi

Binary kilo. Docs list npm and release downloads. kilo.ai/cli/install is served by Kilo but not on the docs page. winget publisher is Kilo Code Inc. Manual download: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/releases. Evidence: https://kilo.ai/docs/cli

OpenCode 2. Arch extra opencode and homebrew-core opencode are 2.x. Vendor docs also name AUR opencode-beta and brew anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2. Vendor states Windows package managers are not supported: winget SST.opencode, scoop main/opencode, choco opencode still ship 1.x. Manual download: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases. Evidence: https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/

Native Windows CLI supported via install.ps1. aiup runs both install scripts without the browser (--skip-browser, -SkipBrowser); Hermes remembers that, and hermes pm install chromium adds it back. Desktop app is a separate MSIX. No official winget (fathah.HermesDesktop is third party). PyPI hermes-agent is not a documented channel. Evidence: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation

Binary warp. Script self-updates. winget Warp.Warp and AUR warp-terminal-bin are the Warp terminal app, and the legacy Oz CLI (oz) uses separate apt/yum/pacman packages. Neither is this CLI. Evidence: https://docs.warp.dev/agents/cli/quickstart/
Requires Python 3.10 to 3.12. No winget (Hotovo.AiderDesk is a third-party GUI). Evidence: https://aider.chat/docs/install.html

Binary goose. self-updates with goose update. winget Pressly.Goose and AUR goose-bin are an unrelated DB migration tool. choco goose not verified as this project, omitted. Evidence: https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/main/documentation/docs/getting-started/installation.md

Binary agent (legacy cursor-agent). winget Anysphere.Cursor is the IDE, not the CLI. Windows install script (not PowerShell, so aiup does not run it): https://cursor.com/install?win32=true. Evidence: https://cursor.com/docs/cli/overview

Arch extra lags npm (0.22 vs 0.26). No winget (Alibaba.Qwen is the chat app). Windows install script (not PowerShell, so aiup does not run it): https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen.bat. Evidence: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code

apt and dnf (yum) from Charm repo repo.charm.sh. Scoop bucket: scoop bucket add charm https://github.com/charmbracelet/scoop-bucket.git. AUR crush is maintained by Charm. choco is community. Manual download: https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush

npm package renamed from @sourcegraph/amp to @ampcode/cli. Docs page shows WSL for Windows, but install.ps1 is served by ampcode.com and winget publisher is Sourcegraph. choco amp is stale, omitted. Evidence: https://ampcode.com/docs/cli
Binary kiro-cli. Requires glibc 2.34+ or musl on Linux, Windows 11. winget Amazon.Kiro and choco kiro are the IDE. Evidence: https://kiro.dev/docs/getting-started/installation/

Binary droid. AUR factory-cli-bin lags (1.0.2 vs npm 1.2.0). winget FactoryAI.Factory is the desktop app. Linux needs xdg-utils. Windows install script (not PowerShell, so aiup does not run it): https://app.factory.ai/cli/windows. Evidence: https://docs.factory.com/cli/getting-started/quickstart
Binary kimi. MoonshotAI.KimiCLI, AUR kimi-cli, scoop kimi-cli, and code.kimi.com/install.sh are the deprecated Python kimi-cli. Evidence: https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code
homebrew-core cline lags npm. winget Cline.ClineDesktop is the desktop app, not the CLI. Evidence: https://github.com/cline/cline
Community adapter, npm is the release channel. Evidence: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-acp
Distro and AUR packages lag (AUR flagged out of date, Debian only in contrib/sid). Evidence: https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/setup.html

Command: fabric (Homebrew names it fabric-ai). Arch extra package fabric is the unrelated Python SSH library. AUR fabric-ai and winget lag behind releases. Manual download: https://github.com/danielmiessler/Fabric/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/danielmiessler/Fabric#installation
Command: sgpt. AUR lags (1.4.4 vs PyPI 1.5.1). Evidence: https://github.com/TheR1D/shell_gpt#installation

Arch also has ollama-cuda, ollama-rocm and ollama-vulkan. Fedora 44 lags (0.12). The ollama snap is a third-party repackage. Manual download: https://ollama.com/download/OllamaSetup.exe. Evidence: https://github.com/ollama/ollama

Linux build is an AppImage that self-updates. flatpak is community-maintained (unverified on Flathub). lmstudio.ai/install.sh installs the headless llmster daemon, not the app. Manual download: Linux https://lmstudio.ai/download/latest/linux/x64, Windows https://lmstudio.ai/download/latest/win32/x64. Evidence: https://lmstudio.ai/download
Flathub app is verified by jan.ai. Releases ship deb and AppImage (x64). Manual download: https://github.com/janhq/jan/releases. Evidence: https://jan.ai/download

Brew formula is macOS-only. On Linux the PyPI extras cuda13, cuda12 or cpu pull the MLX Linux backends. Also on conda-forge. Windows not documented. Command: mlx_lm.generate, mlx_lm.server. CPU only: mlx-lm[cpu]. Evidence: https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm

Linux preview since Aug 2026 (Ubuntu 24.04/26.04, Debian 13, Fedora 43/44, x64 and arm64). The .deb/.rpm from chatgpt.com/download registers the OpenAI repo (persistent.oaistatic.com/codex-app-prod/linux) so updates come through apt/dnf. Binary chatgpt. choco chatgpt is an unrelated unofficial 2024 wrapper. dnf package name comes from vendor docs as reported and was not checked against the rpm repo. Manual download: https://chatgpt.com/download. Evidence: https://developers.openai.com/zh-Hans/docs/linux/linux-app

Linux app is beta and officially supports only Debian 12+ and Ubuntu 22.04+ (x64, arm64) via the apt repo https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-desktop/apt/stable. No rpm (Fedora and Arch users are pointed to the CLI). AUR package is community-maintained. Binary claude-desktop on Linux. winget shows version 2.42304.2 while scoop/choco show 4.4212.0 (the app self-updates after install). Microsoft Store id 9P6K58THS811. Manual download: Linux https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-linux, Windows https://claude.ai/api/desktop/win32/x64/setup/latest/redirect.
Releases ship deb, rpm and AppImage. No apt/dnf repo found. winget GitHub.Copilot is the CLI, not this app. Manual download: https://github.com/github/app/releases.

Linux package is the Personal Computer app from the vendor apt repo packages.perplexity.ai (needs an NVIDIA RTX GPU with 24GB+ VRAM or a DGX Spark). A Windows app exists (Personal Computer for Windows, Jul 2026) but no winget id or direct installer URL could be verified. winget Perplexity.Comet is the Comet browser, a different product. Evidence: https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/products/portable-computer

apt/dnf come from the Microsoft repo packages.microsoft.com. The snap is published by Microsoft. Arch extra/code is the Code - OSS build, not Microsoft VS Code. flatpak is community-maintained. Binary code. Manual download: https://code.visualstudio.com/download. Evidence: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/linux

Same Microsoft apt/dnf repo as stable. The winget manifest lags (1.127) but the app self-updates. Binary code-insiders. Manual download: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/. Evidence: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/setup/linux
Vendor ships deb, rpm and AppImage (x64, arm64) with no documented apt/dnf repo. Windows has user and system installers. Binary cursor. Manual download: https://cursor.com/download.

Zed docs say distro packages (Arch extra, Flathub) are not official. The install script is the documented path. choco zed is an unrelated tool (authzed). Manual download: https://zed.dev/download. Evidence: https://zed.dev/docs/linux
Linux build is a tar.gz (x64, arm64). The old apt/rpm repos carried only legacy 1.x and are no longer updated. Manual download: https://antigravity.google/download.
Releases ship AppImage, deb and tar.gz (x64, arm64) and Windows exe/zip. Manual download: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases.
Nightlies are GitHub prereleases (linux tar.gz x64/arm64, win32 zip). No winget or scoop nightly package found. Manual download: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases.

Desktop app. Linux x64 and arm64 as .deb, .rpm (each registers a signed xAI repo, package grok-bot) or self-updating AppImage. AUR grok-bot-desktop repackages the official .deb. Manual download: https://x.ai/bot. Evidence: https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq

winget and scoop still carry 1.19.5 (v1 line) while the vendor and AUR ship 2.2.5. Flathub ai.opencode.opencode is community-maintained and its product match is unconfirmed. choco opencode is the CLI. Manual download: Linux https://opencode.ai/download/latest/linux-x64-deb, Windows https://opencode.ai/download/latest/windows-x64-nsis. Evidence: https://opencode.ai/download

Vendor ships no Linux desktop package: on Linux the agent installs through the terminal script. The AUR desktop package is a community source build. winget fathah.HermesDesktop is an unrelated third-party app. On Linux the agent itself is the hermes entry. Manual download: https://hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/Hermes-Setup.exe. Evidence: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/desktop

Vendor runs apt, dnf/zypper and pacman repos (releases.warp.dev/linux, pacman section [warpdotdev], package warp-terminal). scoop main/warp and choco warp are unrelated tools. Binary warp-terminal. Manual download: Linux https://app.warp.dev/download?package=appimage, Windows https://www.warp.dev/download. Evidence: https://docs.warp.dev/getting-started/readme/installation-and-setup

No Windows build. Linux packages come from distros (Arch extra, Ubuntu 26.04+ archive). Fedora only via the community COPR scottames/ghostty. The snap is externally maintained. Alternative: wezterm or windows-terminal on Windows. Evidence: https://ghostty.org/docs/install/binary

Linux gets the CLI and server only (no desktop app). Arch also has ollama-cuda, ollama-rocm and ollama-vulkan. The Fedora package lags far behind (0.12.x). The snap is community-maintained. The Windows installer includes the app. Binary ollama. On Linux use the ollama entry. Manual download: https://ollama.com/download/windows. Evidence: https://ollama.com/download
Cross-platform Node CLI. Projects should pin @remotion/cli in their own package.json. Command: remotion. Evidence: https://www.remotion.dev/docs/cli

Vendor says the app runs on macOS, Windows and Linux via the onboarding download. The npm package and brew formula are the CLI (npx screenpipe@latest record). The AUR package is flagged out of date. Manual download: https://screenpi.pe/onboarding. Evidence: https://docs.screenpipe.com/getting-started

Binary vibe. Python 3.12+ (GIL build). AUR is flagged out of date (2.26 vs 3.0.4). Windows works but UNIX is the official target. winget MistralAI.MistralVibe.ACP is ACP mode only. Evidence: https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe

Upstream install doc lists winget for Windows and Homebrew or Nix for Linux. Distro packages trail the daily b-number builds. Release assets include Ubuntu and Windows CPU, CUDA and Vulkan builds. Command: llama-cli, llama-server. Manual download: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/latest. Evidence: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md

Binaries sit on the b-numbered releases (whisper-bin-x64.zip, whisper-bin-ubuntu-x64.tar.gz), not the v tags. choco lags (1.9.2) and Fedora 44 lags (1.8.1). The whisper-cpp snap is third-party. Models are separate. Command: whisper-cli. Manual download: https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp

Fedora ships ffmpeg-free with limited codecs and full ffmpeg comes from RPM Fusion. ffmpeg.org links the gyan.dev and BtbN Windows builds (winget BtbN.FFmpeg.GPL tracks master). The ffmpeg snap is a stale Snapcrafters build. Manual download: Linux https://ffmpeg.org/download.html, Windows https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/.

The vendor AppImage and winget carry Audacity 4 (4.0.1 AppImage, winget 4.0.2) while Arch, Fedora, Flathub and choco are still on 3.7. Flathub (unverified) and snap (Snapcrafters) are community builds. Manual download: Linux https://www.audacityteam.org/download/linux/, Windows https://www.audacityteam.org/download/windows/.
Windows app published by superwhisper. No Linux build. Alternative: handy on Linux. Manual download: https://superwhisper.com/download. Evidence: https://superwhisper.com/

Vendor docs list Flatpak, Snap and AppImage for Linux and the SourceForge installer for Windows. PyPI name is buzz-captions. AUR buzz-bin is an unrelated Block app. Manual download: https://sourceforge.net/projects/buzz-captions/files/. Evidence: https://github.com/chidiwilliams/buzz

The official Linux builds are the verified Flathub app (33.0.1) and the Ubuntu PPA ppa:obsproject/obs-studio. Arch and Debian are on 32.2. The snap is a Snapcrafters build. Manual download: https://obsproject.com/download.

The snap is published by the Blender Foundation (verified) and the Flathub app is community-maintained. LTS lines exist on winget (BlenderFoundation.Blender.LTS.4.5). Manual download: https://www.blender.org/download/.

Vendor names GitHub releases, the Snap Store and Microsoft Store 9P30LSR4705L as the only official channels. Flathub (lags at 3.69.0) and the winget package (third-party publisher) are unofficial. Manual download: https://github.com/mifi/lossless-cut/releases/latest. Evidence: https://github.com/mifi/lossless-cut

The Flathub app is verified by handbrake.fr and is the vendor Linux build. Fedora ships it only through RPM Fusion. The CLI is HandBrake.HandBrake.CLI on winget and main/handbrake-cli on scoop. Command: ghb on Linux. Manual download: https://handbrake.fr/downloads.php.
Flathub (verified) and snap are published by Meltytech. The vendor also ships an AppImage and a portable tarball. Manual download: https://www.shotcut.org/download/.
KDE publishes the Flathub app, the snap and an AppImage. snap (26.04) and choco (26.8.1) lag. Manual download: https://kdenlive.org/download/.
Arch, Fedora and Debian sid ship Krita 6 (6.0.4.1) while Flathub and winget ship 5.3.4.1. The snap is stale (5.2.11). Vendor download is the AppImage. Manual download: https://krita.org/en/download/.
Flathub (verified) and snap are published by the Inkscape project. Ubuntu users can use ppa:inkscape.dev/stable. Debian stable lags. Manual download: https://inkscape.org/release/.

Debian 12 still ships ImageMagick 6 (no magick command) and Debian 13+ ships 7. The vendor also publishes a Linux AppImage. winget ImageMagick.ImageMagick is the Q16-HDRI build. Command: magick. Manual download: https://imagemagick.org/script/download.php.

Releases ship often and distro packages trail (Arch 2026.08.19 vs 2026.10.26). yt-dlp -U only updates the release binary. The snap is third-party. Needs ffmpeg to merge formats. Manual download: https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases/latest. Evidence: https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp
Arch libvips includes the CLI tools. Command: vips, vipsthumbnail. Manual download: https://github.com/libvips/build-win64-mxe/releases. Evidence: https://www.libvips.org/install.html
Binary devin. PowerShell only for setup.ps1. Manual download: https://static.devin.ai/cli/devin-updater-x86_64-pc-windows.exe. Evidence: https://docs.devin.ai/cli
Binary auggie. Evidence: https://docs.augmentcode.com/cli/overview
Binary junie. Docs lead with the install scripts. AUR junie-eap is stale (2144.x vs npm 3110.x), omitted. Evidence: https://junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli.html
Binary letta. AUR lags npm. winget Letta.LettaCode is an installer-based desktop build, not the npm CLI. Evidence: https://github.com/letta-ai/letta-code
Binary qoder. Vendor marks npm as not recommended for new installs. No Windows arm64. Evidence: https://docs.qoder.com/cli/installation
Command: claude-agent-acp. Evidence: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp
Evidence: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/codex-acp
Usually run with npx. Command: mcp-inspector. Evidence: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector
apt and dnf from the vendor repos at mise.jdx.dev (deb and rpm). Snap mise is published by the author (unverified badge). Arch extra lags slightly. Evidence: https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html

apt/dnf repos still live under windsurf-stable.codeiumdata.com and the devin-desktop package replaces windsurf. The Linux tarball does not self-update. winget Codeium.Windsurf and scoop extras/windsurf are the legacy Windsurf 2.3.x line. choco windsurf tracks Devin Desktop. Manual download: Linux https://devin.ai/download/confirmation?code=li, Windows https://devin.ai/download/confirmation?code=wu. Evidence: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/getting-started
Linux downloads are a deb (Debian/Ubuntu 24+) and a universal tar.gz, with no repo. Binary kiro. Manual download: https://kiro.dev/downloads/.
Public Preview. The Linux build is a tar.gz from download.jetbrains.com/air/installers/linux_x64 and Windows is an msix. Manual download: https://www.jetbrains.com/air/. Evidence: https://air.dev/
Releases ship deb, rpm and AppImage (x64, arm64) plus Windows exe/msi. Manual download: https://github.com/generalaction/emdash/releases.

Now named Paradev (formerly Superset). No Windows build. Linux ships deb and AppImage (x64). The superset-sh/superset repo now redirects to ParadevAI/Paradev. Alternative: emdash on Windows. Manual download: https://github.com/ParadevAI/Paradev/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/ParadevAI/Paradev

The desktop app is macOS and Windows only. Alternative: droid (Factory CLI, already a catalog entry) on Linux. Manual download: https://factory.ai/. Evidence: https://factory.ai/news/working-with-droid-in-the-desktop-app
The Antigravity 2 app ships a Linux tar.gz (x64, arm64) from storage.googleapis.com/antigravity-public. The legacy apt/rpm repos are 1.x only. Manual download: https://antigravity.google/download.
The desktop app is macOS and Windows (x64, arm64) only. No Linux build. Manual download: https://gemini.google/desktop/.
Releases ship AppImage, deb and rpm (x64, arm64). The flatpak is unverified on Flathub. Manual download: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/releases.

winget CloudStack.Msty is the older Msty 1.x app (msty.app), not Msty Studio. A Windows arm64 installer is also offered. Manual download: Linux https://next-assets.msty.studio/app/latest/linux/MstyStudio_x86_64.AppImage, Windows https://next-assets.msty.studio/app/latest/win/MstyStudio_x64.exe. Evidence: https://msty.ai/products/studio/
The Linux build is an AppImage from download.chatboxai.app. Manual download: https://chatboxai.app/en/download.
Releases ship AppImage and rpm for the desktop app. Manual download: https://github.com/lobehub/lobehub/releases.
The desktop app is macOS and Windows only. No Linux build. Manual download: https://desktop-app.poecdn.net/downloads/PoeSetup.exe. Evidence: https://poe.com/pages/get-poe

Linux binaries and a launcher AppImage are on GitHub releases. The container images (localai/localai) are the vendor's recommended path on every OS. No native Windows build, so Windows needs Docker. AUR local-ai builds from source. Command: local-ai. Manual download: https://github.com/mudler/LocalAI/releases/latest. Evidence: https://localai.io/docs/installation/
Needs Podman or Docker. Fedora is the vendor's primary distro. On Windows the README says pip install ramalama with Podman Desktop or Docker Desktop. Evidence: https://github.com/containers/ramalama

Apple Silicon first. The PyPI extras cuda and cpu pull the MLX Linux backends and the README covers MLX CUDA. Windows not documented. CPU only: mlx-vlm[cpu]. Evidence: https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-vlm
The standalone PyPI package hf (2.4.0) carries the CLI. Distro huggingface_hub packages lag (Debian 1.23). Command: hf. Evidence: https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli

The same PyPI package works on every OS (Python 3.11 to 3.12) and a Docker image is also documented. winget OpenWebUI.OpenWebUI, Flathub com.openwebui.open-webui and snap open-webui are the separate Open WebUI Desktop app or community builds, not this server. Binary open-webui. Evidence: https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui

Vendor ships .deb, .rpm and AppImage on GitHub releases. The README says the winget package is not maintained by the developers (it is current at 0.10.0). choco lags (0.9.8). AUR handy builds from source. Manual download: https://github.com/cjpais/Handy/releases/latest. Evidence: https://github.com/cjpais/Handy

Official Windows app. No Linux build (the vendor is collecting votes for Linux). AUR wispr-flow-appimage is an unofficial wrapper. Alternative: handy on Linux. Manual download: https://dl.wisprflow.ai/windows/latest. Evidence: https://wisprflow.ai/downloads

Vendor ships StabilityMatrix-linux-x64.zip (AppImage) and StabilityMatrix-win-x64.zip. The README links the AUR package, which is flagged out of date. No winget, scoop or choco package. Manual download: https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/releases/latest. Evidence: https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix

Arch extra/sox is now built from sox_ng (14.8.0.1). Debian sid has sox-ng (14.7). Fedora 44 still ships classic SoX 14.4.2 and only rawhide moved to 14.8.1, so dnf is left blank. scoop main/sox and choco sox.portable are classic SoX 14.4. Command: sox. Manual download: https://codeberg.org/sox_ng/sox_ng/releases. Evidence: https://codeberg.org/sox_ng/sox_ng
Evidence: https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix#quick-start
AUR flagged out of date. Evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown#installation
Binary muse. npm @muse-code/sdk is the SDK, not the CLI. Evidence: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code
Binary mcode. winget MiniMax.MiniMaxCode is the NSIS desktop app, not the npm CLI. AUR lags npm. Evidence: https://agent.minimax.io/docs/cli/quick-start
Binary codebuddy. winget Tencent.CodeBuddy is the IDE. AUR lags npm. Evidence: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tencent-ai/codebuddy-code

Formerly DeepSeek TUI. winget id is under the original author's name but downloads from codewhale-hq releases. Manual download: https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/releases. Evidence: https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale
